programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Finn agus Georgia còmhla rithe ‘s iad ag ullachadh burgairean glasrach. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil na stuthan a tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha ola an lus-ola a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson na burgairean ullachadh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd gan ithe. Linda Macleod and friends prepare a number of tasty dishes. She is joined by Finn and Georgia to make mouthwatering veggie burgers. Before they start cooking, there is a check for ingredients and they go shopping for any that are missing. Linda and her friends also learn more about where rapeseed oil comes from. They return to the kitchen to make the burgers before sitting down at the table to tuck in.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh a’ cur cafaidh air chois. Tha uallach orra nach tig duine dhan chafaidh aca, ach chan fheum uallach sam bith a bhith orra! Abney and Teal decide to set up a café. They're worried about not getting any customers, but they have no reason to be concerned.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Dè tha ceàrr air na bèibidhean seilcheag an-diugh - is dè na slighean dealrach a tha sin? What are the baby snails up to today, and what are these shiny trails?

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Sand! Sea! Worms! Stan and Gran must quickly discover where all these worms came from or Ellie's new clothes drying service will be ruined! Gainmheach! Muir! Boiteagan! Feumaidh Dan is Gran co-dhùnadh gu luath, cò às a thàinig na tha seo de bhoiteagan, no thèid an t-seirbheis ùr 'son tioramachadh aodaich aig Eilidh, à bith!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ leughadh Mo Chreach a Sheòrais! Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Chris Haughton, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. Coinneach Rankin reads Mo Chreach a Sheòrais! Written and illustrated by Chris Haughton, it was translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl is a charaidean air an taghadh airson sgioba ball-coise na sgoile a bhrosnachadh, le bhith a’ gairm às leth na sgoile. Le cuideachadh bho Ghranaidh, tha iad gus an taisbeanadh as fheàrr a chur air dòigh airson sgoil a’ bhaile. Dave and his friends are enlisted as cheerleaders for their school sports team. With the help of Gran they are going to put on the best, and only, cheer performance their Grimsby school has ever seen.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Beileag a’ toirt clup uabhasach do Phòl ro dhiosgo bliadhnail na coimhearsnachd, is mar sin feumaidh e falt-fuadain a chur air. Gu mì-fhortanach, tha seo a’ toirt cruth-atharrachaidh air Pòl. Betty gives Dave a bad haircut ahead of the annual community disco, so Dave has to wear a wig. Unfortunately, his new stylish hairpiece comes with a few side effects.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Air an slighe gu Fèill Geamhraidh Throlberg, tha Hilda, Flòraidh is Daibhidh a’ tighinn tarsainn air daoine beaga èibhinn, a tha a’ lorg clann a tha rasgach. Ach carson? On their way to the Trolberg Winter Festival, Hilda, Flòraidh and Daibhidh come across funny little characters, who are looking for naughty children. But why?

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Bekah! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha i ag innse dhuinn mu rionnagan agus a’ sealltainn cuid de na dealbhan mìorbhaileach a chaidh a thogail ann am fànas. Blast off into space with astronaut Bekah! In this amazing space voyage, she tells us all about stars and shows us some of the astounding images taken in space.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek Murray hosts a fun knockout amateur DIY competition where couples go head to head. Derek Moireach le farpais spòrsail DIY is cupail a’ strì an aghaidh a chèile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na h-ath cheumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Tha Maria Robasdan à Obar Dheathain a’ tadhal air Joy san stiùidio agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ cur air a bhrògan dannsaidh airson Bhangra fheuchainn le buidheann ann an Dùn Èideann. Joy Dunlop guides us through the next steps to speak Gaelic. Learner Maria Robertson from Aberdeen chats to Joy in the studio, and Calum Maclean dons his dancing shoes as he tries out Bhangra dancing in Edinburgh. Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Se latha geamaichean Uibhist a Deas a th’ann agus tha farpais iasgaich ann am Barraigh. A fishing competition is held in Barra, while Highland dancers compete at the South Uist games.

programme.title: An Cogadh Fuar: Cold War Stories
programme.desc: Stories of how the Cold War impacted the lives of ordinary people. Sgeulachdan mu mar a thug an Cogadh Fuar buaidh air beatha dhaoine àbhaisteach.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Ross Miller Band, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2025. A’ gabhail a-steach The Dedication Jigs agus The Drunken Man from Kalabakan. Concert set performed by the Ross Miller Band, originally recorded live at the Trad Awards, 2025. Featured tracks include The Dedication Jigs and The Drunken Man from Kalabakan.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Triathlon Innse Gall a’ leantainn dithis bhon aon teaghlach agus iad a’ cur romhpa an dùbhlan spòrs as motha nam beatha fheuchainn. ’S e seo a’ chiad triathlon do Luke MacAoidh agus bràthair-athar, Hector, agus iad a’ farpais an aghaidh a chèile agus trichead farpaiseach eile air slighe spòrs nach dìochuimhnich iad a chaoidh. As dèidh fad mhìosan a’ trèanadh, seiseanan snàimh sa mhoch-mhadainn agus ruith is rèiseadh air baidhsagal fhad ’s a tha a’ ghrian a’ dol fodha – an dèan duine dhen dithis aca a’ chùis air là mòr Triathlon Innse Gall? Hebrides Triathlon follows the journey of two Lewis men who throw themselves head, and feet first, into the sporting challenge of their lives. For Luke MacKay and his uncle, Hector, it was a first ever triathlon as they competed against one another, and 30 others, in a sporting experience they will never forget. After several months of training, early morning open water swimming sessions and leg-sapping runs and cycles in the fading sun - will they both manage to complete the highly-anticipated Hebrides Triathlon? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay, baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile, agus sin gun ghuth air cail ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha na caroaich agus muinntir a bhail a'toirt an aghaidh air a cheile ach caite am faighear buachaille a dh' fhagas gach taobh ann an deagh fhonn? Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere on the fringes of the map. The town is overrun with sheep, and local dignitaries are stumped until a stranger appears over the horizon.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Sreath spioradail le measgachadh de laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. Cluinnear laoidhean air an clàradh as ùr agus cuideachd feadhainn bhon tasglann a chaidh a chlàradh beagan bhliadhnaichean air ais. Bidh Pàdruig Moireasdan agus Seonaidh Ailig MacGuaire a’ leughadh bhon sgrioptar agus bidh Iain MacFhionghain a’ leughadh earrann bho na Cosamhlachdan. Anns a’ phrògram cluinnear Iseabail Anna Mhàrtainn a’ seinn Salm 51, an laoidh Spiorad Naoimh Dhè air a sheinn le Dòmhnall-Iain MacIlleDhuinn agus bhon tasglann Ruairidh Gray le Do Dhia Biodh a’ Ghlòir. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings. He reads a parable and introduces hymns and psalms - some recorded especially for Alleluia! and others taken from the rich collection of previous performances. Isobel Anne Martin sings Psalm 51, Donald-Iain Brown recites Spiorad Naoimh Dhè and there is another opportunity to appreciate performances from the archive, including Ruairidh Gray singing Do Dhia Biodh a’ Ghlòir. Pàdruig Morrsion and John Alex MacQuarrie reflect on their chosen reading from the Bible. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Summer of '76: Away from It All
programme.desc: Herbie and June Harris and their children waited all year to go on holiday. But quite unexpectedly, Herbie lost his job, and Stephen, their eldest, left school and couldn't find work. Despite their misfortunes, the Harris family were determined to go through with the holiday, rather than disappoint the boys and the other families going with them. Herbie and June tell their own story of the summer of 1976 - how they coped with their problems, learnt the value of friends and discovered the importance of making the best of things - away from it all.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. The Polymaths pool their disparate skills in chicken husbandry, musical theatre and urban geography to challenge the brainpower of the Strategists, a team unified by their love of sophisticated strategy board games. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, including Cakes and Ale, The Dogs of War, Brave New World and The Darling Buds of May.

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: Simon Schama tackles the 20th century through the lives of two men - Winston Churchill and George Orwell. Both men, so very different in almost every way, lived through and wrote about the key moments of British 20th-century life - the Depression, Empire, two world wars and the Cold War. What unites them, argues Schama, is one shared theme - forget history at your peril.

programme.title: The American Revolution
programme.desc: American colonists oppose efforts by the British Crown and Parliament to seize greater control in North America, escalating simmering tensions over land, taxes and sovereignty into a violent confrontation. After protesters dump tea in Boston Harbor, the British government enacts martial law in Massachusetts. Fighting at Lexington and Concord ignites a war that will last eight years. A film by Ken Burns, Sarah Botstein and David Schmidt.

programme.title: The American Revolution
programme.desc: New Englanders rush to surround the British Army in Boston, but as war begins, Americans find themselves sharply divided. After the Battle of Bunker’s Hill, George Washington of Virginia arrives to command the newly created Continental Army. In July 1776, the Continental Congress issues the Declaration of Independence, insisting on the people’s right to resist tyranny and govern themselves. A film by Ken Burns, Sarah Botstein and David Schmidt.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: As the World Cup kicks off who's cashing in and who's paying up? 2026 is set to be Fifa's most lucrative tournament ever with billions being earnt from tv rights and sponsorship deals as well as controversially high ticket prices. So how do broadcasters and sponsors make their huge investments pay-off? Ricardo Fort helps companies advertise at leading sports tournaments and shares his insights from his time as head of sponsorships at Visa and Coca-Cola. And as streaming giant Dazn tries to change the way the world watches live sport its CEO of Growth Markets, who oversees its football rights, Pete Oliver explains how new technology is changing viewing habits. Plus, Ben Thompson also hears from leading sports consultant Tony Simpson, from Oliver Wyman, about how these big tournaments boost economies and can leave a lasting legacy.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

Former police inspector Anton Sullivan test-drives trackable tech to see if it’s worth the hype. And victims of a serial thief tell how their doorbell footage eventually brought him to justice.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A double fatal shooting leads to an island-wide search for evidence, an elderly man has collapsed on the roadside, and a makeshift machete is found amongst squatters' belongings.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team face up against one of the cruellest and most terrifying scams they have ever seen – scammers posing as the National Crime Agency to frighten their targets into believing they will be arrested if they don’t prove their identity by buying gift cards. These scammers even spoof the numbers of genuine police stations and use props to make their targets believe they face arrest if they don’t comply. As the hub team try to prevent one man losing out, the ground team track down the shop that the man has been sent to so he can purchase the cards. But will they find him in time?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton is in the East Riding of Yorkshire with a couple heading home after a life in France, along with their dog Daisy and a serious craving for family, friends and proper fish and chips. With £280,000 to spend, they explore a tempting mix of characterful older homes and smart modern properties. Along the way, Alistair also learns about a local scheme helping to create affordable housing so local people can continue to put down roots in this much-loved corner of the county.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam are in Waterlooville to transform Jackie and Alan’s overgrown and out-of-control patch into a garden inspired by their love of Spain. They lived in the country, so they would love a garden that reflects their time there, with Mediterranean planting. Low maintenance is a must for their retirement. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Annie’s home is packed with inherited hoards. JB finds a rare classic, while Lauren uses a food staple for a clever fix to boost an item’s sale for Annie’s beloved charity.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group I between France and Senegal from the New Jersey Stadium in New York. France almost won back-to-back World Cups in Qatar four years ago but lost on penalties against Argentina, after perhaps the greatest World Cup final in history had finished 3-3. Senegal were involved in controversy earlier this year when they beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal had earlier walked off after their opponents were awarded a controversial penalty and the result was later overturned with Morocco declared the winners. France are among the favourites to win the tournament but Senegal did produce one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history when they famously beat Les Bleus in 2002.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team face up against one of the cruellest and most terrifying scams they have ever seen – scammers posing as the National Crime Agency to frighten their targets into believing they will be arrested if they don’t prove their identity by buying gift cards. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright meets a group of doorbell detectives from Hampshire who combined the latest tech with doorbell footage to catch a burglar red-handed. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan test-drives trackable tech to see if it’s worth the hype. And victims of a serial thief tell how their doorbell footage eventually brought him to justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion wants to tear down a bungalow in Staffordshire, but the planners might have a different idea! Martel is in Grimsby, where the layout in a flat conversion is confusing. And Martin travels to Buckinghamshire, where a flat looks, potentially, like a great deal, but is there a sting in the tail?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles heads to Norwich for today's episode. Experts Raj Bisram and Stephanie Connell are on hand to help the teams as they compete to make the most profit at auction. Eric visits Norwich City Football Club to discover the history behind football chanting.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A double fatal shooting leads to an island-wide search for evidence, an elderly man has collapsed on the roadside, and a makeshift machete is found amongst squatters' belongings.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team face up against one of the cruellest and most terrifying scams they have ever seen – scammers posing as the National Crime Agency to frighten their targets into believing they will be arrested if they don’t prove their identity by buying gift cards. These scammers even spoof the numbers of genuine police stations and use props to make their targets believe they face arrest if they don’t comply. As the hub team try to prevent one man losing out, the ground team track down the shop that the man has been sent to so he can purchase the cards. But will they find him in time?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton is in the East Riding of Yorkshire with a couple heading home after a life in France, along with their dog Daisy and a serious craving for family, friends and proper fish and chips. With £280,000 to spend, they explore a tempting mix of characterful older homes and smart modern properties. Along the way, Alistair also learns about a local scheme helping to create affordable housing so local people can continue to put down roots in this much-loved corner of the county.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam are in Waterlooville to transform Jackie and Alan’s overgrown and out-of-control patch into a garden inspired by their love of Spain. They lived in the country, so they would love a garden that reflects their time there, with Mediterranean planting. Low maintenance is a must for their retirement. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Annie’s home is packed with inherited hoards. JB finds a rare classic, while Lauren uses a food staple for a clever fix to boost an item’s sale for Annie’s beloved charity.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Lucy Porter for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: East Midlands Today
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the East Midlands.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Alex Jones and Roman Kemp bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group I between France and Senegal from the New Jersey Stadium in New York. France almost won back-to-back World Cups in Qatar four years ago but lost on penalties against Argentina, after perhaps the greatest World Cup final in history had finished 3-3. Senegal were involved in controversy earlier this year when they beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal had earlier walked off after their opponents were awarded a controversial penalty and the result was later overturned with Morocco declared the winners. France are among the favourites to win the tournament but Senegal did produce one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history when they famously beat Les Bleus in 2002.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: East Midlands Today
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the East Midlands.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group I between France and Senegal from the New Jersey Stadium in New York. France almost won back-to-back World Cups in Qatar four years ago but lost on penalties against Argentina, after perhaps the greatest World Cup final in history had finished 3-3. Senegal were involved in controversy earlier this year when they beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal had earlier walked off after their opponents were awarded a controversial penalty and the result was later overturned with Morocco declared the winners. France are among the favourites to win the tournament but Senegal did produce one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history when they famously beat Les Bleus in 2002.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

France almost won back-to-back World Cups in Qatar four years ago but lost on penalties against Argentina, after perhaps the greatest World Cup final in history had finished 3-3. Senegal were involved in controversy earlier this year when they beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal had earlier walked off after their opponents were awarded a controversial penalty and the result was later overturned with Morocco declared the winners. France are among the favourites to win the tournament but Senegal did produce one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history when they famously beat Les Bleus in 2002.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Points West
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the West of England.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group G as Iran take on New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium. Iran, appearing at their seventh World Cup, are looking to make it past the group stage for the first time. They return four years on from featuring at Qatar 2022, where they beat Wales 2-0 in between defeats to England and the United States. There had been uncertainty over Iran’s participation at the 2026 edition because of the war with the US and Israel, which began just over three months before the start of the tournament. New Zealand make their return to the World Cup 16 years on from going unbeaten in 2010, though draws with Slovakia, Paraguay and Italy weren’t enough to make it past the group stage. Nottingham Forest’s Chris Wood played in 2010, and much of the nation’s hopes will rest on their captain and record goalscorer this time around if they are to progress to the knockouts for the first time.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team face up against one of the cruellest and most terrifying scams they have ever seen – scammers posing as the National Crime Agency to frighten their targets into believing they will be arrested if they don’t prove their identity by buying gift cards. These scammers even spoof the numbers of genuine police stations and use props to make their targets believe they face arrest if they don’t comply. As the hub team try to prevent one man losing out, the ground team track down the shop that the man has been sent to so he can purchase the cards. But will they find him in time?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton is in the East Riding of Yorkshire with a couple heading home after a life in France, along with their dog Daisy and a serious craving for family, friends and proper fish and chips. With £280,000 to spend, they explore a tempting mix of characterful older homes and smart modern properties. Along the way, Alistair also learns about a local scheme helping to create affordable housing so local people can continue to put down roots in this much-loved corner of the county.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam are in Waterlooville to transform Jackie and Alan’s overgrown and out-of-control patch into a garden inspired by their love of Spain. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.desc: Alistair Appleton is in the East Riding of Yorkshire with a couple heading home after a life in France, along with their dog Daisy and a serious craving for family, friends and proper fish and chips. With £280,000 to spend, they explore a tempting mix of characterful older homes and smart modern properties. Along the way, Alistair also learns about a local scheme helping to create affordable housing so local people can continue to put down roots in this much-loved corner of the county.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam are in Waterlooville to transform Jackie and Alan’s overgrown and out-of-control patch into a garden inspired by their love of Spain. They lived in the country, so they would love a garden that reflects their time there, with Mediterranean planting. Low maintenance is a must for their retirement. Can the team achieve all this on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group I between France and Senegal from the New Jersey Stadium in New York. France almost won back-to-back World Cups in Qatar four years ago but lost on penalties against Argentina, after perhaps the greatest World Cup final in history had finished 3-3. Senegal were involved in controversy earlier this year when they beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal had earlier walked off after their opponents were awarded a controversial penalty and the result was later overturned with Morocco declared the winners. France are among the favourites to win the tournament but Senegal did produce one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history when they famously beat Les Bleus in 2002.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: The opening day of live action in Group I sees Iraq take on Norway in Boston. Iraq were the final team to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, beating Bolivia in a play-off held in Mexico in April. Star striker Aymen Hussein scored the winning goal in that game to fulfil his ambition to reach a World Cup with Iraq, 40 years after the country’s first and only appearance at the tournament in 1986. It has been 28 years since Norway last featured at a World Cup in France in 1998, but they qualified in style, topping their group and registering two victories over four-time winners Italy. All eyes will be on their prolific Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who scored 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Odegaard of Arsenal.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: On the remote island of Papa Westray, the Baker family need to pregnancy scan their 64 ewes, but their flock is running amok. They have timed lambing to happen after Mel has her baby, which is due imminently. With no hospital facilities on the island, the entire family prepare to leave for mainland Orkney. In Dumfries and Galloway, Nick and his dad Derek are in the thick of lambing and calving. Nick is exhausted from lambing his dad’s traditional flock, and as night falls, a calf’s life hangs in the balance. At Hillhead Farm, Ben is back to help with lambing, while eldest son Matt takes prospective clients to visit the hilltop event site in the middle of an amber weather warning. Keziah returns home in time for a visit from a group of nursery kids, who get an impromptu biology lesson.

programme.title: Reported Missing

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: OnlyFans: Inside the Machine
programme.desc: Behind the billion-pound success of OnlyFans lies a hidden ecosystem of exploitation. A BBC Current Affairs investigation uncovers allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed by some of the hundreds of agents who manage many of the platform’s creators as well as the potential for modern slavery. Through survivor testimony, undercover access to a managers’ chat forum and expert legal analysis, the film exposes an industry where young women are trapped, threatened and profited from - raising urgent questions about accountability at the heart of one of Britain's most lucrative tech companies.

programme.title: Santa Claus: The Serial Killer
programme.desc: Journalist Mobeen Azhar travels to Canada to investigate the mysterious cases of men who went missing from Toronto’s gay village. It was the summer of 2017, just one day after Toronto’s annual Pride parade, and a dark shadow fell over the city’s gay area. As the street parties faded away, one man had vanished. His name was Andrew Kinsman. Mobeen looks into what happened and finds that Andrew was a popular guy in the area who was known to keep a regular schedule. Andrew’s friends organised search parties, but it gradually became clear his face was not the only one on missing person posters across the village. There was another man. Mobeen meets the detective who led the police’s hunt for answers. They initially struggled for leads, but finally they had an unlikely breakthrough. A clue left by Andrew himself. When the suspect gets exposed, it sends shockwaves through the tight-knit community.

programme.title: Santa Claus: The Serial Killer
programme.desc: Journalist Mobeen Azhar continues his investigation into the story behind the murders of eight men in Toronto. On a wintery morning in 2018, police made a chilling discovery. Nestled in the garden of a quaint house in deep suburbia were answers to the mysterious cases of men that had gone missing in the city. Mobeen heads to what became an unprecedented crime scene and is granted access to this crucial location by the homeowners. They are still dealing with the aftermath of police knocking on their door looking for bodies. The case of this prolific serial killer never went to full trial, and Mobeen, like a lot of people in the city, has unanswered questions. Why did Bruce McArthur, a shopping mall Santa Claus, choose a couple’s garden as his burial site? After he’s confronted by the traumatic end to the victims’ lives, Mobeen takes his investigation back to the start. What made McArthur single out these men? Two sources linked to the village suggest the killer might have been targeting strangers. Mobeen tracks down friends of the first-known victim, Skandaraj Navaratnam, who was murdered back in 2010.

programme.title: Santa Claus: The Serial Killer
programme.desc: A married father of two from a neighbourhood on the outskirts of Toronto leaves for work one day and never returns. The mystery deepens when his car is found on the other side of the city in a quiet neighbourhood. There are no answers and two years later, another man disappears. Both missing men were originally from Afghanistan and like the first victim, Skanda, they were also brown-skinned. Journalist Mobeen Azhar investigates what led serial killer and shopping mall Santa Claus Bruce McArthur to target these men, tracking down an out-of-town retired cop who provides a disturbing insight into the missing person investigation related to one of these men years earlier.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: On a Bradford estate, Lenny and Mullet find an abandoned car and turn it into a DIY spaceship. A kitchen-sink science fiction comedy about estate childhoods, big dreams and escaping without going anywhere.

At the end of their journey, an extraordinary feast awaits - if he can run the gauntlet without his babies becoming someone else’s meal.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Margherita Taylor and Adam Henson explore a side of the Isle of Wight few visitors ever see. Beyond the beaches and bustling holiday towns, the island’s rare geology and southerly location have shaped a landscape rich in surprises, from unusual marine life and distinctive habitats to crops more often associated with warmer climates.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Week two of Springwatch begins with another packed line-up of wildlife stories and live camera action from across the UK. Presenters Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan uncover the dramatic moments captured over the weekend by the live cameras at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. This programme explores the remarkable adaptations of some of Britain’s best-loved woodland birds, whilst Iolo Williams heads into the heart of London to reveal the unexpected wildlife thriving in the capital.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Rotherham, 25-year-old sports fanatic Kerry dreams of becoming a Paralympian after a skiing accident changed her life. Roman Kemp wants to introduce her to an unlikely ally: the humble beetroot. Studies show that beetroot can boost fitness performance and enhance brain power. It is a vibrant vegetable with serious athletic potential.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: To celebrate a summer of women’s sport, Christina Trevanion captains a contest of cricket versus tennis! Former British number ones Jo Durie and Samantha Smith are Team Tennis. They take on Team Cricket, made up of trailblazing broadcaster Alison Mitchell and cricketing all-rounder and commentator Melissa Story. Coached by antiques experts Ben Cooper and Danny Sebastian, the teams are quick off the baseline to bag some bargains at a bustling antiques fair in Shepton Mallet, Somerset. The reds plan to smash their sporting challenge with what Ben identifies as ship’s rudder, but it doesn’t float their boat. Later, Sam picks up the pace when she spots a vintage pedometer. Over with the cricketing blues, a reel-to-reel tape player takes Alison back to her early broadcasting days, and at another stall, they consider whether to convert a rugby ball-shaped decanter into a sale.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent are in Water Orton to help Johnny and Jo transform their uneven, overgrown garden, neglected for 60, maybe 70 years, into a stunning blend of rustic French charm and English Victorian elegance. The couple want to keep an old ivy as a central feature, alongside fragrant lavender, honeysuckle and jasmine to attract wildlife. Sustainability is key, with reclaimed brick for raised beds and walkways, and recycled wooden reels repurposed for tables. A gin-and-tonic pergola, cosy seating area and hidden garden nooks will add charm and character throughout the space. Married for 31 years, Johnny and Jo first met when he was a chef and she his manager. Their journey took them to France, raising two boys before returning to the UK. Now retired, they have poured their hearts into restoring a former sweet shop and general store into a home full of character – and they’re ready to do the same for the garden. Can the team bring this historic plot back to life with a modern twist on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In County Down, dairy farmer Derek Geddis turns to a volunteer search and rescue team after three of his cattle go missing. When the animals are found stranded in a river, the farmer’s skills and the team’s technology are put to the test in a delicate recovery mission. As daylight fades, the pressure mounts to bring the herd to safety. In County Durham, a community support officer’s drone footage helps catch deer poachers in the act. His quick response and aerial evidence lead to a rare conviction, highlighting how modern policing is tackling traditional countryside crimes. And in North Wales, reporter Paul Colgan investigates how police and scientists are using dog DNA to trace the animals behind devastating livestock attacks – a breakthrough that could bring long-awaited justice to farmers.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The scuba team take on the search for a son’s precious last gift from his late father... but with such a vast area to cover, will they be successful? Elsewhere, the freedivers and detectorists head to the natural pools at Buttermere for a clean-up and are surprised to find something of great value.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Queen's Tennis
programme.desc: Live coverage from day 9 of the 2026 Queen's tennis tournament.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Ben Bailey Smith, Robin Ince, Lara Ricote and Helen Skelton take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s rail journey continues on the Bergen Line, heading towards the Norwegian capital of Oslo. Carving through the mountains across some of Europe’s most inhospitable terrain, he passes glaciers, lakes, waterfalls and plateaux to reach northern Europe’s highest station at 1,200 meters above sea level. He marvels at the feat of engineering required to build the line, which runs for 300 miles through more than 180 tunnels. Arriving in Oslo, Michael admires its fine modernist architecture and 19th-century parliament building. In Telemark, he visits Vemork power station, scene of one of the greatest stories of wartime heroism. The son of one of the heroes of Telemark tells the story. Michael enjoys a heritage rail ride in Rjukan and discovers a medieval stave church in Heddal.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson investigates how a Cornish gem became world-famous for tin. In the bay, the archaeologist unravels the epic story behind the hundreds of huge carved stones that lie scattered in the surf. There's a look at some medieval technology in action at one of the oldest tin refineries in Britain, and a local doctor consults his ancestor’s 150-year-old medical diary for evidence of past ailments.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Walford rallies behind Jack and Denise. A familiar face returns to the Square. Vinny makes a declaration to Penny.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: Professor Alice Robert explores exciting archaeological finds from the west of Britain. Every new discovery was filmed by the archaeologists themselves, giving us an unprecedented view of each excavation as it happens. In this episode, we join a team as they undertake the largest maritime investigation since the Mary Rose and reveal the extraordinary story of HMS Invincible. At Silchester, archaeologists investigate a bath house that reveals how the Romans stamped their mark on Britain. A buried military camp in Hampshire shows why German soldiers were key to our security in the 18th century, and archaeologist Raksha Dave goes behind the scenes to tell the tragic tale of individuals from a 19th-century pauper’s graveyard.

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: Amanda is given a devastating cancer diagnosis. Her community and church rally around her as she inspires thousands more with a blog, bravely chronicling her journey

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: As an investigative reporter looks closer at Amanda's story, the cracks begin to show. And while Amanda continues to blog and fundraise, suspicion spreads.

programme.title: It Happened to Me
programme.desc: A 2000ft fall off a jagged mountain ridge should have been fatal. Instead, one endurance runner survived the drop and managed to run four miles to find his own rescue on a Scottish island.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Brexit: A Very British Civil War
programme.desc: Cameron and his chancellor George Osborne are convinced the way to win is by highlighting the economic cost of leaving the EU. But their first intervention falls flat, as Vote Leave sends their new messenger Boris Johnson around the country on a bus that claims Britain sends the EU £350 million a week. Meanwhile, Nigel Farage is running a separate leave campaign focused on immigration. Despite refusing to confront immigration head-on, Cameron chooses to share a platform with Nigel Farage.

In this episode, we join a team as they undertake the largest maritime investigation since the Mary Rose and reveal the extraordinary story of HMS Invincible. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Margherita Taylor and Adam Henson explore a side of the Isle of Wight few visitors ever see. Beyond the beaches and bustling holiday towns, the island’s rare geology and southerly location have shaped a landscape rich in surprises, from unusual marine life and distinctive habitats to crops more often associated with warmer climates.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Week two of Springwatch begins with another packed line-up of wildlife stories and live camera action from across the UK. Presenters Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan uncover the dramatic moments captured over the weekend by the live cameras at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. This programme explores the remarkable adaptations of some of Britain’s best-loved woodland birds, whilst Iolo Williams heads into the heart of London to reveal the unexpected wildlife thriving in the capital.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Rotherham, 25-year-old sports fanatic Kerry dreams of becoming a Paralympian after a skiing accident changed her life. Roman Kemp wants to introduce her to an unlikely ally: the humble beetroot. Studies show that beetroot can boost fitness performance and enhance brain power. It is a vibrant vegetable with serious athletic potential.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: To celebrate a summer of women’s sport, Christina Trevanion captains a contest of cricket versus tennis! Former British number ones Jo Durie and Samantha Smith are Team Tennis. They take on Team Cricket, made up of trailblazing broadcaster Alison Mitchell and cricketing all-rounder and commentator Melissa Story. Coached by antiques experts Ben Cooper and Danny Sebastian, the teams are quick off the baseline to bag some bargains at a bustling antiques fair in Shepton Mallet, Somerset. The reds plan to smash their sporting challenge with what Ben identifies as ship’s rudder, but it doesn’t float their boat. Later, Sam picks up the pace when she spots a vintage pedometer. Over with the cricketing blues, a reel-to-reel tape player takes Alison back to her early broadcasting days, and at another stall, they consider whether to convert a rugby ball-shaped decanter into a sale.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent are in Water Orton to help Johnny and Jo transform their uneven, overgrown garden, neglected for 60, maybe 70 years, into a stunning blend of rustic French charm and English Victorian elegance. The couple want to keep an old ivy as a central feature, alongside fragrant lavender, honeysuckle and jasmine to attract wildlife. Sustainability is key, with reclaimed brick for raised beds and walkways, and recycled wooden reels repurposed for tables. A gin-and-tonic pergola, cosy seating area and hidden garden nooks will add charm and character throughout the space. Married for 31 years, Johnny and Jo first met when he was a chef and she his manager. Their journey took them to France, raising two boys before returning to the UK. Now retired, they have poured their hearts into restoring a former sweet shop and general store into a home full of character – and they’re ready to do the same for the garden. Can the team bring this historic plot back to life with a modern twist on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In County Down, dairy farmer Derek Geddis turns to a volunteer search and rescue team after three of his cattle go missing. When the animals are found stranded in a river, the farmer’s skills and the team’s technology are put to the test in a delicate recovery mission. As daylight fades, the pressure mounts to bring the herd to safety. In County Durham, a community support officer’s drone footage helps catch deer poachers in the act. His quick response and aerial evidence lead to a rare conviction, highlighting how modern policing is tackling traditional countryside crimes. And in North Wales, reporter Paul Colgan investigates how police and scientists are using dog DNA to trace the animals behind devastating livestock attacks – a breakthrough that could bring long-awaited justice to farmers.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The scuba team take on the search for a son’s precious last gift from his late father... but with such a vast area to cover, will they be successful? Elsewhere, the freedivers and detectorists head to the natural pools at Buttermere for a clean-up and are surprised to find something of great value.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome little ones Dionne, Holly, Reau, Francis, Oliver and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside Nigel’s bag are a red skittle, a red fire engine toy and a red ball, and all the parents and babies have different objects and toys that are red. These are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding a safe, baby appropriate red toy or object inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular baby song Little Robin Redbreast features, as does a story involving Baby Bear and Baby Tiger, and viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring red things too. The Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with sensory bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and a group of children make pretend cakes, learn British Sign Language signs for pat, cake and baby, and sing and sign the rhyme Pat-a-Cake.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Chocolate maker Ali shows the Fact Pack a real cacao pod. They discover where chocolate really comes from, how cacao beans change as they are fermented and dried, and how they become tasty chocolate.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: A visit from older zebra Bahati leads the baby zebras into mischief. Hamza spots some wild warthogs and takes on a smelly but useful task at the orphanage!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger races the Baby Pea-Rexes around Vegesaur Valley to the water hole.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: A quick trip to the shops proves tricky for Dad, when Bingo and Bluey want to play a game of 'Kids'. Now Bluey is Mum, and Bingo is her baby. For Dad however, he is a very naughty boy.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is encouraging the Squirrels to come outside by gesturing through the window. They don’t understand what he’s doing and think it’s funny. When he comes inside, a bit exasperated, he explains that he was miming. They want to know what miming is, and Duggee fondly recalls his days as a young Parisian street performer. The Squirrels are keen to learn how to mime, and Duggee runs them through the basics.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Blue and Yellow meet a new friend - Green. Discover what happens when you mix blue and yellow.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Harper has lots of questions about beautiful butterflies! Ferne visits a butterfly farm and gets up close and personal with lots of amazing butterflies. She even helps feed them, but she has to find them first! Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy plant some lovely wild flowers to attract butterflies to the garden. Also, we find out why butterflies are so important to the environment by being great pollinators of different crops.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: When Henry and his family go on a trip to a nearby pond, it’s fishing nets at the ready as they try their hand at a spot of shrimping! It’s not easy as the tiny shrimp are good at hiding. Luckily, Henry comes up with a plan – but will it work? And will they catch any shrimp? Later, it’s Henry who is good at hiding in a family game of hide-and-seek. But will his clever hiding place be discovered?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Jessica's family is from Ukraine - part of a region is known for a soup called borscht, and Jessica will be making some for her friends. Jessica cooks cabbage and spring onions in oil and then adds them to grated carrot, beetroot, potatoes and a tomato and stock mixture. These ingredients are combined in a casserole dish. Once they are stirred together, the dish can be placed in the oven. Jessica wears a traditional Ukrainian outfit and serves drinks in a beautiful drinks dispenser. Borscht is famous for being brightly coloured, so will her friends be able to guess that her special ingredient is beetroot?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In this episode, Maddie is in the garden. She finds out how spiders make webs using silk, meets a spider expert and learns that different spiders make different types of webs. Using her slow-motion camera, Maddie shows how a garden spider makes an orb web. We learn that the structure is built in a special way so that it is strong and sticky but light. Next Maddie heads to a factory where watering cans are made. We learn how a watering can starts out as a lot of flat metal shapes. Maddie shows us how they are bent and moulded into all the different parts. She uses her special slow-motion camera to show how electromagnetic paint is sprayed and how it sticks to the metal watering can, making it smooth and shiny.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Meagaidh the Border Collie is a search and rescue dog who works with her owner Tom. Her supernose follows scents and smells like clues, so they can rescue people who need their help. Joe and his daughter Kate are in trouble at the top of a really steep hill. They are lost, cold, soggy, tired and hungry. And they’ve dropped their picnic bag down a hill. Joe manages to contact Tom at the Woofton Search and Rescue Centre, just before the battery on his phone runs out. Now, Tom and Meagaidh must race to find them! Meagaidh leads the way, avoiding the sheep, the muddy puddles and the rocks. She soon finds Joe’s picnic bag, which gives her and Tom the scent they need. Together, they set off up the hill to find Joe and Kate. Just wait until Dog Squad hears about their adventure!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet Stan, the striated caracara. Stan is a supersmart bird. He reveals his problem-solving skills as he searches for food hidden in pots and puzzle boxes. Next, they meet some wolverines. Wolverines are members of the weasel family and are known for their feisty and determined nature. They live in the Arctic, where there is lots of snow and prey is hard to come by. They can travel large distances - about 25km per day - to try to find food. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba finds a beautiful, shiny shell that causes some seagull trouble for Oona.

programme.title: Small Potatoes

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs

But luckily, Uncle George knows some more ways they can bid farewell - without actually saying goodbye.

programme.title: Hey Duggee

They learn about sound waves, and that you can listen for different qualities in the sounds, such as if it’s loud, quiet, high or low. Describing the sound can help you work out where it’s coming from, so Duggee lets the Squirrels close their eyes as they listen to sounds and make their guesses.

programme.title: Numberblocks

This episode introduces the letter M and the words mat, map and man.

programme.title: Something Special

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: In Teletubbyland Dipsy is King. Tinky Winky delivers Tubby Custard and Tubby Toast to King Dipsy - whatever he wants!

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 220 million years to the time of cynodont - a dog-like furry creature with excellent eyesight and a powerful sense of smell. His mission is to find some lichen, a moss-like plant that cynodont used as bedding in its underground burrow. Along the way he meets coelophysis, one of the earliest dinosaurs and one of cynodont's deadliest enemies. But, will Andy succeed in time before the museum opens?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses a pair of walkie-talkies and remembers the day she got them. When Caitlin accidentally breaks Moira’s Big Hub walkie-talkie, Mack and Bob are drafted in to help her. But with the broken walkie-talkie still in Moira’s office, ‘Sneaky Mack’, ‘Undercover Caitlin’ and ‘Fixer Bob’ need to figure out how to get it from the office and fix it before Moira gets back from her break. Soon, a heist-like mission is under way. But keeping anything quiet from the suspicious Moira is not going to be easy. Once the intrepid three have got hold of, and fixed, the walkie-talkie, they breathe a sigh of relief. But it’s not long before Moira confronts them, and ‘Sneaky Mack’, ‘Undercover Caitlin’ and ‘Fixer Bob’ have a confession to make.

MeMo and BaBa have gentle, snoring breaths when they drift off to sleep.

Inside Nigel’s bag are a red skittle, a red fire engine toy and a red ball, and all the parents and babies have different objects and toys that are red. These are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding a safe, baby appropriate red toy or object inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular baby song Little Robin Redbreast features, as does a story involving Baby Bear and Baby Tiger, and viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring red things too. The Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with sensory bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and a group of children make pretend cakes, learn British Sign Language signs for pat, cake and baby, and sing and sign the rhyme Pat-a-Cake.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Chocolate maker Ali shows the Fact Pack a real cacao pod. They discover where chocolate really comes from, how cacao beans change as they are fermented and dried, and how they become tasty chocolate.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: A visit from older zebra Bahati leads the baby zebras into mischief. Hamza spots some wild warthogs and takes on a smelly but useful task at the orphanage!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger races the Baby Pea-Rexes around Vegesaur Valley to the water hole.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: A quick trip to the shops proves tricky for Dad, when Bingo and Bluey want to play a game of 'Kids'. Now Bluey is Mum, and Bingo is her baby. For Dad however, he is a very naughty boy.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is encouraging the Squirrels to come outside by gesturing through the window. They don’t understand what he’s doing and think it’s funny. When he comes inside, a bit exasperated, he explains that he was miming. They want to know what miming is, and Duggee fondly recalls his days as a young Parisian street performer. The Squirrels are keen to learn how to mime, and Duggee runs them through the basics.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Blue and Yellow meet a new friend - Green. Discover what happens when you mix blue and yellow.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Harper has lots of questions about beautiful butterflies! Ferne visits a butterfly farm and gets up close and personal with lots of amazing butterflies. She even helps feed them, but she has to find them first! Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy plant some lovely wild flowers to attract butterflies to the garden. Also, we find out why butterflies are so important to the environment by being great pollinators of different crops.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: When Henry and his family go on a trip to a nearby pond, it’s fishing nets at the ready as they try their hand at a spot of shrimping! It’s not easy as the tiny shrimp are good at hiding. Luckily, Henry comes up with a plan – but will it work? And will they catch any shrimp? Later, it’s Henry who is good at hiding in a family game of hide-and-seek. But will his clever hiding place be discovered?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Jessica's family is from Ukraine - part of a region is known for a soup called borscht, and Jessica will be making some for her friends. Jessica cooks cabbage and spring onions in oil and then adds them to grated carrot, beetroot, potatoes and a tomato and stock mixture. These ingredients are combined in a casserole dish. Once they are stirred together, the dish can be placed in the oven. Jessica wears a traditional Ukrainian outfit and serves drinks in a beautiful drinks dispenser. Borscht is famous for being brightly coloured, so will her friends be able to guess that her special ingredient is beetroot?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In this episode, Maddie is in the garden. She finds out how spiders make webs using silk, meets a spider expert and learns that different spiders make different types of webs. Using her slow-motion camera, Maddie shows how a garden spider makes an orb web. We learn that the structure is built in a special way so that it is strong and sticky but light. Next Maddie heads to a factory where watering cans are made. We learn how a watering can starts out as a lot of flat metal shapes. Maddie shows us how they are bent and moulded into all the different parts. She uses her special slow-motion camera to show how electromagnetic paint is sprayed and how it sticks to the metal watering can, making it smooth and shiny.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Meagaidh the Border Collie is a search and rescue dog who works with her owner Tom. Her supernose follows scents and smells like clues, so they can rescue people who need their help. Joe and his daughter Kate are in trouble at the top of a really steep hill. They are lost, cold, soggy, tired and hungry. And they’ve dropped their picnic bag down a hill. Joe manages to contact Tom at the Woofton Search and Rescue Centre, just before the battery on his phone runs out. Now, Tom and Meagaidh must race to find them! Meagaidh leads the way, avoiding the sheep, the muddy puddles and the rocks. She soon finds Joe’s picnic bag, which gives her and Tom the scent they need. Together, they set off up the hill to find Joe and Kate. Just wait until Dog Squad hears about their adventure!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet Stan, the striated caracara. Stan is a supersmart bird. He reveals his problem-solving skills as he searches for food hidden in pots and puzzle boxes. Next, they meet some wolverines. Wolverines are members of the weasel family and are known for their feisty and determined nature. They live in the Arctic, where there is lots of snow and prey is hard to come by. They can travel large distances - about 25km per day - to try to find food. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba finds a beautiful, shiny shell that causes some seagull trouble for Oona.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of singing potatoes. The Small Potatoes explore different jobs, from firemen to astronauts, in this disco pageant.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Sonny finds an old line-dancing record, Yukee thinks it would be a mighty swell idea if the gang had a line dance in the Sunhouse. But remembering the moves proves a problem for the gang, can Yukee find a way to help them?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: When Maddie and Triggs realise it's time for Uncle George to go, they do everything they can to stop him from leaving - it's been such a fun holiday, and they don't want it to stop! But luckily, Uncle George knows some more ways they can bid farewell - without actually saying goodbye.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After hearing a strange sound, the Squirrels turn to Duggee to help identify its source. They learn about sound waves, and that you can listen for different qualities in the sounds, such as if it’s loud, quiet, high or low. Describing the sound can help you work out where it’s coming from, so Duggee lets the Squirrels close their eyes as they listen to sounds and make their guesses.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One, Two, Three and Four are off on a castle-exploring adventure, with a little help from the friends they make along the way. Learn how to make numbers up to ten by adding with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. M is very hungry, so he and his friends make a gingerbread man - but he runs off. They chase on a flying mat, and a handy map keeps them hot on his trail. Can they corner the cheeky biscuit? This episode introduces the letter M and the words mat, map and man.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Dominic to get ready for the day, sharing some cereal and brushing her teeth. Sorting out old toys makes Mr Tumble feel sleepy. There's a jumble sale in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words cereal, toothbrush and sleepy.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: In Teletubbyland Dipsy is King. Tinky Winky delivers Tubby Custard and Tubby Toast to King Dipsy - whatever he wants!

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 220 million years to the time of cynodont - a dog-like furry creature with excellent eyesight and a powerful sense of smell. His mission is to find some lichen, a moss-like plant that cynodont used as bedding in its underground burrow. Along the way he meets coelophysis, one of the earliest dinosaurs and one of cynodont's deadliest enemies. But, will Andy succeed in time before the museum opens?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses a pair of walkie-talkies and remembers the day she got them. When Caitlin accidentally breaks Moira’s Big Hub walkie-talkie, Mack and Bob are drafted in to help her. But with the broken walkie-talkie still in Moira’s office, ‘Sneaky Mack’, ‘Undercover Caitlin’ and ‘Fixer Bob’ need to figure out how to get it from the office and fix it before Moira gets back from her break. Soon, a heist-like mission is under way. But keeping anything quiet from the suspicious Moira is not going to be easy. Once the intrepid three have got hold of, and fixed, the walkie-talkie, they breathe a sigh of relief. But it’s not long before Moira confronts them, and ‘Sneaky Mack’, ‘Undercover Caitlin’ and ‘Fixer Bob’ have a confession to make.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that all use the wind to move! First, Grace heads to an airfield to fly a glider. Then, she shows off the amazing solar orbiter and hits the beach to drive a kite buggy!

programme.title: BeddyByes

MeMo and BaBa have gentle, snoring breaths when they drift off to sleep.

Suddenly the Ninky Nonk stops and won't go. Upsy Daisy wonders why - then realises that the Ninky Nonk wants a kiss too.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Reece's driving lesson with Disneyland Darren quickly descends into chaos, but beneath the madness Darren reveals a surprising need to be a father figure. At school, Mia-Louise lands a football academy place but clashes with disciplined teammate Daisy, whose professionalism exposes Mia-Louise's attitude problems. Aimee attends a high-stakes audition for a Cilla Black musical with Mr Dunn, but class prejudice makes her question whether she belongs. When Darren arranges a secret hookup at the same hotel, Reece and Christopher mistakenly believe Dunn is cheating on Jodie. Their attempt to expose him spirals into farce, sending an angry husband to the wrong room and triggering absurd misunderstandings. Amid the chaos, Aimee finds her voice in the audition while Mia- Louise's prank video goes viral, threatening her football future.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Reece's driving lesson with Disneyland Darren quickly descends into chaos, but beneath the madness Darren reveals a surprising need to be a father figure. At school, Mia-Louise lands a football academy place but clashes with disciplined teammate Daisy, whose professionalism exposes Mia-Louise's attitude problems. Aimee attends a high-stakes audition for a Cilla Black musical with Mr Dunn, but class prejudice makes her question whether she belongs. When Darren arranges a secret hookup at the same hotel, Reece and Christopher mistakenly believe Dunn is cheating on Jodie. Their attempt to expose him spirals into farce, sending an angry husband to the wrong room and triggering absurd misunderstandings. Amid the chaos, Aimee finds her voice in the audition while Mia- Louise's prank video goes viral, threatening her football future.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Reece's driving lesson with Disneyland Darren quickly descends into chaos, but beneath the madness Darren reveals a surprising need to be a father figure. At school, Mia-Louise lands a football academy place but clashes with disciplined teammate Daisy, whose professionalism exposes Mia-Louise's attitude problems. Aimee attends a high-stakes audition for a Cilla Black musical with Mr Dunn, but class prejudice makes her question whether she belongs. When Darren arranges a secret hookup at the same hotel, Reece and Christopher mistakenly believe Dunn is cheating on Jodie. Their attempt to expose him spirals into farce, sending an angry husband to the wrong room and triggering absurd misunderstandings. Amid the chaos, Aimee finds her voice in the audition while Mia- Louise's prank video goes viral, threatening her football future.

Ex-covert operative Bryan Mills' long-awaited reconciliation with his ex-wife is tragically cut short when she is brutally murdered - consumed with rage and framed for the crime, he goes on the run to evade the relentless pursuit of the CIA, FBI and the police. Bryan must use his 'particular set of skills' for one last time to track down the real killers, exact his unique brand of justice, and protect the only thing that matters to him now - his daughter.

programme.title: American Dad!
